title: MAPPED: Explore the Essex UFO sighting hotspots with our interactive map
excerpt: An interactive map of the mysterious objects sightings hotspots across Essex.
content:
STRANGE lights hovering over Basildon, mysterious objects around Stansted Airport and unusual formations above Colchester are among the UFO sightings reported across Essex.

An interactive Echo map plots reports recorded by Essex Police, showing the hotspots across Essex and what has been spotted.

The records range from balls of light and metallic objects to formations later linked to satellites, aircraft and flares.

Basildon, Southend, Chelmsford and Colchester have multiple reports, while several intriguing incidents cluster around Stansted Airport.

Use the map to find your area, then tap or click a marker to see what was reported and its possible explanation.

Strange lights over Basildon

Basildon features some of the police records’ strangest descriptions.

One report described a dim ball of light moving in and out of clouds, changing speed and hovering.

Other reports described a large square object with red and green lights, plus streams a caller likened to burning drones or a flare.

But map clusters do not mean Basildon is uniquely prone to unexplained phenomena.

Where police records name only a town, we have spaced the markers apart so readers can see and select each report.

Why Stansted?

The cluster around Stansted Airport may have a straightforward explanation - there is a lot happening in the sky.

In 2015, someone reported seeing four or five lights from the Saffron Walden area towards the airport.

Police checks found five aircraft waiting to land nearby at the time.

Other incidents are less straightforward.

In 2022, aircraft approaching Stansted Airport reportedly received collision avoidance alerts relating to an object approximately 500 feet below them, although pilots were unable to see it.

In 2023, an airside worker reported a large green cylinder moving slowly against the runway direction.

When Starlink looks like a UFO

Mysterious - Many sightings have been linked to satellite launches (Image: Provided)

Not every strange sight in Essex’s night sky is an aircraft.

Starlink satellites can provide particularly spectacular sightings because shortly after launch they can appear as a procession of bright, evenly spaced lights moving across the sky.

Their unusual appearance means these so-called satellite trains are often mistaken for UFOs.

Essex has numerous examples.

In 2020, groups of lights were spotted travelling silently in a straight line near Ongar.

Police records suggested the lights may have been Starlink satellites.

The UFO sightings that had an explanation

Some mysteries were solved quickly.

Explore - Dozens of sightings have been reported in the night sky (Image: PA)

Large golden-orange lights reported above Colchester in 2024 were confirmed as flares.

Three purple flashing lights over Southend were thought most likely to have come from an Adventure Island light show.

Other possible explanations included meteors, planets, drones, helicopters and aircraft.

In 2008, lights reported over Billericay were traced to the Sky Bar's rooftop skytracker equipment.

Does the map really show Essex's UFO hotspots?

Not quite.

The map shows where unusual objects were reported to police, not where unexplained aerial phenomena happen most often.

Densely populated areas have more potential witnesses, while busy flight paths put more aircraft and lights in view.

Coastal areas also offer relatively clear views towards the horizon, making distant lights easier to spot.

A UFO report is not evidence of alien activity.

Essex Police says it records UFO incidents for policing reasons: an unidentified object could be an aircraft in distress or linked to illegal activity.

The records show what Essex residents saw when they looked up, and how some baffling sightings turned out to have an earthly explanation.
